title: Graded Carbohydrate Ingestion up to 120 g/h Attenuates the Reduction in Critical Power Following 3 h of Moderate-Intensity Exercise in a Dose-Dependent Manner
authors: Norte BR, Slinn MM, Johnson KO, Mahon E, Shepherd SO, Strauss JA, Louis JB
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
population: Endurance-trained cyclists/triathletes (n = 16; VO2max 51.8 +/- 6.8 mL/kg/min), 3 h cycling at 95% gas exchange threshold
findings: Water vs 60 vs 120 g/h CHO (maltodextrin:fructose 1:0.8) after a standardised 24 h CHO load (8 g/kg) and a 2 g/kg pre-exercise meal.
Critical power (end-test power) fell from 277 +/- 27 W unfatigued to 236 +/- 30 (water), 257 +/- 28 (60 g/h) and 266 +/- 29 W (120 g/h); reduction attenuated dose-dependently (p < 0.05).
W' declined over time with no differences between fatigued conditions.
Whole-body CHO oxidation 1.84, 2.16 and 2.31 g/min for water, 60 and 120 g/h.
limitations: n = 16 cyclists, 3 h, no running, GI outcomes not in the abstract, not ultra-distance; durability inferred from a critical-power surrogate; crossover design inferred from the multi-condition protocol, not stated in the abstract.
implications: Supports the idea that fatigue resistance depends on in-event CHO dose; may justify higher targets for moderate-to-high intensity efforts over 3 h within tolerance.
Do not generalise to low-intensity ultra racing; keep 120 g/h as an optional tier requiring training tolerance.
